decisions.reason: As a plug-in product directly extending the firm's core geospatial integration and software-component business, it is a low-cost option to keep open and there is not yet enough post-launch evidence to justify abandonment.

The building digital twin service fits the firm's geospatial-enterprise integration direction, but as a newer and more solution-intensive offer its market uncertainty is higher, so it should be retained while demand becomes clearer.

Authentication and identity delegation is strategically adjacent to the firm's integration work but somewhat less central than its geospatial core, so management would likely keep it for now while watching whether customer uptake justifies further commitment.

An open GIS application development framework matches the firm's open, extensible and user-centered positioning well, making it a promising option whose value is still too uncertain to close after only a short time on the market.

The GIS-focused identity and access service supports seamless GeoIT integration and was explicitly presented as a new offering, so despite some overlap risk with other identity-related options it is still worth keeping on the market for another year.
